summary: Configured the repo to surface Windows Rust prerequisites clearly, installed rustup and wasm32-wasip2 on the Windows host, and confirmed the remaining blocker is the missing MSVC linker (link.exe).
timeline: Checked the Rust build path used by the Zed extension installer.
Confirmed cargo builds successfully inside WSL.
Installed Rustup on the Windows host with winget.
Added the wasm32-wasip2 target on the Windows host.
Verified cargo build now fails on Windows because link.exe is missing.
Updated repo docs and doctor checks to mention the Windows C++ build-tools requirement.
decisions: Treat the install failure as an environment problem, not a Rust source bug.
Add Windows-specific diagnostics for the missing linker rather than changing the Rust extension entrypoint.
Document that Windows Zed needs Visual Studio Build Tools with the C++ workload.
issues: Visual Studio Build Tools installation via winget exited with code 1602 in this environment.
Windows cargo build still fails until link.exe is available.
npm run doctor from a Windows shell over the WSL UNC path is unreliable because cmd.exe does not handle the current directory cleanly.
next_steps: Install Visual Studio Build Tools with the C++ build tools workload on the Windows host, or run Zed inside WSL instead of Windows.
Re-run the dev-extension install after link.exe is present.
Optionally add a small Windows-path note to the README for UNC/WSL workspace setups.
